subQuestions.label: 1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
The table shows the time spent ($x$, in minutes) by shoppers at a clothing store and the amount of money ($y$, in Rands) they spent:

| Time spent ($x$) | 27 | 41 | 45 | 51 | 60 | 53 | 35 |
| Money spent ($y$) | 400 | 630 | 700 | 1 040 | 1 200 | 870 | 745 |

Use your calculator to determine the equation for the line of best fit in the form $y = A + Bx$. Give your answer correct to 3 decimal places.

subQuestions.label: 1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Predict how much an individual would spend if they were in the clothing store for 90 minutes. Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

subQuestions.label: 1(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Is the prediction in Question (b) a reliable one? Explain.
subQuestions.memoText: No. It is not reliable — this is extrapolation (working outside the boundaries of the given data), which carries risks.

subQuestions.label: 1(d)
subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the correlation coefficient for the data. Give your answer correct to 3 decimal places.

subQuestions.label: 1(e)
subQuestions.questionText: What does the correlation coefficient suggest about the relationship between the time spent in a clothing store and the money spent by the individual?
subQuestions.memoText: A very strong positive correlation.

subQuestions.label: 2(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram gives the ogive (cumulative frequency) curves for the heights of two groups of plants: 200 plants in Environment A and 200 in Environment B. For Environment A, the minimum height is 2 cm and the maximum is 68 cm.

Draw a box-and-whisker plot that represents the height of plants in Environment A.
subQuestions.memoText:
Reading the five-number summary from the Environment A ogive:
Min $= 2$; $Q_1 = 30$; $Q_2$ (median) $= 44$; $Q_3 = 52$; Max $= 68$.
Draw the box-and-whisker plot accordingly. (Maximum 2 marks if the box-and-whisker plot contains errors.)

subQuestions.label: 2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: If the mean height of the plants in Environment B is given as 34 cm, describe the skewness of the data represented by the Environment B curve.
subQuestions.memoText: Skewed left / negatively skewed.

subQuestions.label: 2(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Under which environment were the heights of the plants more spread out? Explain.
subQuestions.memoText: Environment A. Since Range A > Range B and $\text{IQR}_A > \text{IQR}_B$, the heights of the plants grown in Environment A were more spread out.

questions.title: Analytical Geometry — Lengths, Gradients & Similar Triangles

subQuestions.label: 3(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
In the diagram, points $A(6; 16)$, $B(11; 12)$, $E(6; -11)$ and $D(-4; -3)$ are given. AE intersects DB at the point $C(6; k)$.

Calculate the length of AB.

subQuestions.label: 3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Show that AB // DE.
subQuestions.memoText:
$m_{AB} = \dfrac{16 - 12}{6 - 11} = -\dfrac{4}{5}$
$m_{DE} = \dfrac{-11 - (-3)}{6 - (-4)} = \dfrac{-8}{10} = -\dfrac{4}{5}$
The gradients are equal, so AB // DE.

subQuestions.label: 3(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the value of $k$.
subQuestions.memoText:
$m_{DB} = \dfrac{12 - (-3)}{11 - (-4)} = 1$
Equation of DB: $y = x + c$; using $D(-4; -3)$: $-3 = -4 + c \Rightarrow c = 1$, so $y = x + 1$.
At $x = 6$ (the $x$-coordinate of C): $y = 7$.
$\therefore k = 7$

subQuestions.label: 3(d)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the size of $B\hat{A}C$.
subQuestions.memoText:
$m_{AB} = -\dfrac{4}{5}$; the acute angle its line makes with the horizontal is $\theta \approx 38{,}7°$ (from $\tan\theta = \tfrac{4}{5}$).
AE is vertical ($A$ and $E$ both have $x = 6$), so $AC \perp$ $x$-axis, i.e. its inclination is $90°$.
$B\hat{A}C = 180° - (90° + 38{,}7°) = 51{,}3°$ (interior angles of the triangle).

subQuestions.label: 3(e)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine $\dfrac{\text{Area of } \triangle ABC}{\text{Area of } \triangle EDC}$.
subQuestions.memoText:
$\triangle ABC \;|||\; \triangle EDC$ (equiangular: $\hat{D} = \hat{B}$ — alternate angles, AB // DE; vertically opposite angles at C).
$DE = \sqrt{(6 - (-4))^2 + (-11 - (-3))^2} = \sqrt{100 + 64} = \sqrt{164} = 2\sqrt{41}$.
$\dfrac{\text{Area } \triangle ABC}{\text{Area } \triangle EDC} = \left(\dfrac{AB}{DE}\right)^2 = \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{41}}{2\sqrt{41}}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{4}$

subQuestions.label: 4(a)(1)
subQuestions.questionText:
In the diagram, AB is a diameter of a circle with $A(2; 8)$ and $B(1; -1)$.

Determine the length of AB.

subQuestions.label: 4(a)(2)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the equation of the circle.
subQuestions.memoText:
Centre $=$ midpoint of AB $= \left(\dfrac{2 + 1}{2}; \dfrac{8 - 1}{2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{3}{2}; \dfrac{7}{2}\right)$.
$r = \dfrac{\sqrt{82}}{2}$
$\left(x - \dfrac{3}{2}\right)^2 + \left(y - \dfrac{7}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{41}{2}$

subQuestions.label: 4(a)(3)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the equation of the tangent to the circle at A.
subQuestions.memoText:
$m_{\text{diam}} = \dfrac{8 - (-1)}{2 - 1} = 9$, so $m_{\text{tan}} = -\dfrac{1}{9}$.
$y = -\dfrac{1}{9}x + c$; using $A(2; 8)$: $8 = -\dfrac{2}{9} + c \Rightarrow c = 8\dfrac{2}{9}$.
$y = -\dfrac{1}{9}x + 8\dfrac{2}{9}$  (or $9y = -x + 74$)

subQuestions.label: 4(b)
subQuestions.questionText:
The circle $x^2 + y^2 = 100$ is drawn. M is the point $(13; 0)$ and MA is a tangent to the circle.

Determine the length of the tangent AM. Leave your answer in surd form.
subQuestions.memoText:
Construct OA. $OA = 10$ units (radius), and $OA \perp AM$ (tangent $\perp$ radius).
$(AM)^2 = (13)^2 - (10)^2 = 69$  (Pythagoras)
$AM = \sqrt{69}$

subQuestions.label: 5(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Given $f(x) = \cos 2x$ and $g(x) = \tan x + 2$ for $x \in [-180°; 90°]$.

Sketch the graphs of $f$ and $g$ on the same set of axes. Label all intercepts with the axes, asymptotes, turning points and end points.
subQuestions.memoText:
$f(x) = \cos 2x$: period $180°$, amplitude 1. Turning points at $x = -180°$ (max), $-90°$ (min), $0°$ (max), $90°$ (min). $x$-intercepts at $x = -135°, -45°, 45°$. $y$-intercept $(0; 1)$. End points $(-180°; 1)$ and $(90°; -1)$.
$g(x) = \tan x + 2$: vertical asymptote at $x = -90°$. $x$-intercept where $\tan x = -2$, at $x \approx -63{,}4°$. $y$-intercept $(0; 2)$. End point $(-180°; 2)$.
Marks: $f$ shape and end points; $f$ turning points; $f$ $x$-intercepts; $g$ shape and end points; $g$ asymptote; $g$ $x$-intercept $(-63{,}4°)$. Do not penalise twice for incorrect end points.

subQuestions.label: 5(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Use your graph to determine the approximate value(s) of $x \in [-180°; 90°]$ for which $\cos 2x - 2 \leq \tan x$.
subQuestions.memoText:
$\cos 2x - 2 \leq \tan x$ rearranges to $\cos 2x \leq \tan x + 2$, i.e. $f(x) \leq g(x)$:
$x \in [-180°; -90°) \cup [-70{,}1°; 90°)$
(Allow a range of $[-65°; -75°]$ for the intersection point read from the graph.)

questions.title: Circle Geometry — Angle at the Centre; Tangents

subQuestions.label: 6(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Use the diagram to prove the theorem that states that the angle subtended by a chord at the centre of a circle is twice the size of the angle that it subtends at the circle.

Required to prove: $A\hat{O}C = 2 \times A\hat{B}C$.
subQuestions.memoText:
Construction: draw BO produced (B through the centre O).
Proof: $\hat{O}_1 = \hat{A}_1 + \hat{B}_1$ (exterior angle of a triangle).
$\hat{A}_1 = \hat{B}_1$ (isosceles triangle — radii equal).
$\therefore \hat{O}_1 = 2\hat{B}_1$.
Similarly, in the other triangle: $\hat{O}_2 = 2\hat{B}_2$.
Adding: $A\hat{O}C = \hat{O}_1 + \hat{O}_2 = 2(\hat{B}_1 + \hat{B}_2) = 2 \times A\hat{B}C$.

subQuestions.label: 6(b)(1)
subQuestions.questionText:
A, B and C lie on the circle with centre O. TC and TA are tangents to the circle with $C\hat{T}A = 62°$.

Determine $\hat{A}_1$. State all relevant reasons with your statements.
subQuestions.memoText:
$\hat{C}_1 = \hat{A}_1$ (tangents from a common point / isosceles triangle TCA).
$2\hat{A}_1 + \hat{T} = 180°$ (interior angles of $\triangle$).
$2\hat{A}_1 + 62° = 180°$
$\hat{A}_1 = 59°$

subQuestions.label: 6(b)(2)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine $\hat{O}_1$.
subQuestions.memoText:
$\hat{A}_1 + \hat{A}_2 = 90°$ (radius $\perp$ tangent).
$\hat{A}_2 = 90° - 59° = 31°$.
$\hat{A}_2 = \hat{C}_2$ (isosceles $\triangle$; CO = AO radii).
$\therefore \hat{O}_1 = 180° - 31° - 31° = 118°$ (interior angles of $\triangle$).
(Alternatively: $\hat{A}_1 = \hat{B}$ (tan-chord theorem); $\hat{O}_1 = 2 \times 59° = 118°$ — angle at centre $= 2 \times$ angle at circle.)

subQuestions.label: 7(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
In the diagram, $\triangle$AOC and $\triangle$ABC are given. D lies on OA and E on AC with DE // OC. F lies on AB with EF // CB. H and G lie on AC with HF // GB. AO = 7 units and AD = 4 units.

Determine the ratio of AF : FB, giving reasons.
subQuestions.memoText:
$DO = 7 - 4 = 3$, so $AD : DO = 4 : 3$.
$\dfrac{AD}{DO} = \dfrac{AE}{EC} = \dfrac{AF}{FB}$ (proportion theorem — DE // OC and EF // CB).
$\therefore AF : FB = 4 : 3$

subQuestions.label: 7(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the ratio of GB : HF, giving reasons.
subQuestions.memoText:
$\triangle AHF \;|||\; \triangle AGB$ (equiangular).
$\dfrac{AH}{AG} = \dfrac{HF}{GB} = \dfrac{AF}{AB}$ (similar triangles, sides in proportion).
With $AF = 4x$ and $FB = 3x$, $AB = 7x$, so $\dfrac{HF}{GB} = \dfrac{4x}{7x}$.
$\therefore GB : HF = 7 : 4$

subQuestions.label: 7(c)
subQuestions.questionText: If it is further given that G is the midpoint of EC, determine the ratio AE : EG, giving reasons.
subQuestions.memoText:
$AE : EC = 4 : 3$ (proportion theorem).
With $EC = 3k$: $EG = GC = 1\tfrac{1}{2}k$ (G is the midpoint of EC).
$\therefore AE : EG = 4 : \dfrac{3}{2}$  or  $8 : 3$

subQuestions.label: 8(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Solve for $x$, correct to one decimal place, in the given interval:

$$\sin 3x = -\dfrac{3}{4} \quad \text{for } x \in [-90°; 0°]$$

subQuestions.label: 8(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the general solution for $\tan x = \sin 2x$ if $\sin x \neq 0$.
subQuestions.memoText:
$\dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x} = 2\sin x\cos x$
$\sin x = 2\sin x\cos^2 x$
$2\sin x\cos^2 x - \sin x = 0$
$\sin x(2\cos^2 x - 1) = 0$
Since $\sin x \neq 0$: $2\cos^2 x - 1 = 0$, i.e. $\cos 2x = 0$.
$2x = \pm 90° + k\cdot 360°$, $k \in \mathbb{Z}$
$\therefore x = \pm 45° + k\cdot 180°$, $k \in \mathbb{Z}$

subQuestions.label: 9(a)
subQuestions.questionText: If $\sin\hat{C} = \dfrac{12}{13}$ where $0° < C < 90°$ and $\tan\hat{D} = -\dfrac{4}{3}$ where $270° < D < 360°$, determine $\sin(C - D)$ without the use of a calculator.
subQuestions.memoText:
$\cos C = \dfrac{5}{13}$ (C in Quadrant 1).
$\sin D = -\dfrac{4}{5}$ and $\cos D = \dfrac{3}{5}$ (D in Quadrant 4).
$\sin(C - D) = \sin C\cos D - \cos C\sin D = \left(\dfrac{12}{13}\right)\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right) - \left(\dfrac{5}{13}\right)\left(-\dfrac{4}{5}\right) = \dfrac{56}{65}$

subQuestions.label: 9(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Given $\cos 58° = k$, express $\cos 150° \cdot \cos(-28°) + \cos 60° \cdot \cos 62°$ in terms of $k$ without the use of a calculator.

subQuestions.label: 10(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
ACD is a triangular field on horizontal ground. E is a point on AD. BC is a vertical building. $AC = 80$ m and $ED = 53$ m. $C\hat{A}E = 60°$ and $C\hat{E}A = 45°$.

Calculate the length of CD.
subQuestions.memoText:
In $\triangle AEC$: $\dfrac{EC}{\sin 60°} = \dfrac{80}{\sin 45°}$
$EC = \dfrac{80\sin 60°}{\sin 45°} \approx 98$ m.
In $\triangle EDC$: $C\hat{E}D = 180° - 45° = 135°$ (adjacent angles on a straight line).
$(CD)^2 = (53)^2 + (97{,}98)^2 - 2(53)(97{,}98)\cos 135°$
$CD \approx 140{,}5$ m

subQuestions.label: 10(b)
subQuestions.questionText: If the angle of elevation of B from A is 37°, determine the angle of elevation of the midpoint of BC from D.
subQuestions.memoText:
In $\triangle ACB$: $\tan 37° = \dfrac{BC}{AC} \Rightarrow BC = 80\tan 37° = 60{,}284$ m.
Let M be the midpoint of BC: $MC = \dfrac{1}{2}BC = 30{,}142$ m.
In $\triangle DMC$: $\tan(C\hat{D}M) = \dfrac{MC}{CD} = \dfrac{30{,}142}{140{,}55}$
$C\hat{D}M \approx 12{,}1°$
The angle of elevation of M from D is $12{,}1°$.

questions.title: Analytical Geometry — Two Circles in a Block

subQuestions.label: 11(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
$P(x; y)$ and $Q(9; 3)$ are the centres of two holes drilled into a rectangular piece of wood with base ABCO. The radii of the holes are equal. The equation of the circle with centre P is $x^2 + y^2 - 6x - 12y + 41 = 0$. The equations of AB and BC are $y = 10$ and $x = 14$ respectively.

Determine the centre and the radius of the hole with centre P.

subQuestions.label: 11(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the shortest distance between the circles. Leave your answer in surd form.
subQuestions.memoText:
$PQ = \sqrt{(9 - 3)^2 + (3 - 6)^2} = \sqrt{45} = 3\sqrt{5}$
Shortest distance $= PQ - (r_P + r_Q) = 3\sqrt{5} - (2 + 2) = 3\sqrt{5} - 4 \approx 2{,}7$

subQuestions.label: 11(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the volume of the block with base ABCO and height 20 units.
subQuestions.memoText:
Volume of block $= lbh - 2 \times (\pi r^2 h)$
$= (20 \times 14 \times 10) - 2\left(\pi(4)(20)\right)$
$= 2\,800 - 160\pi$
$\approx 2\,297{,}3$ units$^3$

questions.title: Statistics — Mean & Standard Deviation in Terms of Variables

subQuestions.label: 12(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
A set of 10 numbers consists of five values equal to $a$ and five values equal to $b$, where $a > b$.

Determine the mean in terms of $a$ and $b$.
subQuestions.memoText: $\bar{x} = \dfrac{5a + 5b}{10} = \dfrac{a + b}{2}$

subQuestions.label: 12(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the standard deviation in terms of $a$ and $b$.
subQuestions.memoText:
$\sigma^2 = \dfrac{5\left(a - \dfrac{a + b}{2}\right)^2 + 5\left(b - \dfrac{a + b}{2}\right)^2}{10} = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{a - b}{2}\right)^2 + \left(\dfrac{b - a}{2}\right)^2}{2} = \dfrac{(a - b)^2}{4}$
$\sigma = \dfrac{a - b}{2}$  (since $a > b$)

questions.title: Circle Geometry — Cyclic Quadrilaterals & Tangent Length

subQuestions.label: 13(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
O is the centre of the circle. Chords AD and CB intersect at E, and AC // BD.

Prove that AEOB is a cyclic quadrilateral.
subQuestions.memoText:
Let $\hat{O}_1 = 2x$.
$\therefore \hat{D} = x$ (angle at centre $= 2 \times$ angle at circle).
$\therefore \hat{A}_1 = x$ (alternate angles; AC // BD).
$\therefore \hat{C} = x$ (angles in the same segment).
In $\triangle CAE$: $\hat{E}_1 = 180° - 2x$ (interior angles of $\triangle$).
$\therefore \hat{E}_2 = 2x$ (adjacent angles on a straight line).
Since $\hat{E}_2 = 2x = \hat{O}_1$, and these angles are subtended by AB, AEOB is a cyclic quadrilateral (angles in the same segment equal).

subQuestions.label: 13(b)
subQuestions.questionText:
A, B, C, D and E lie on the circle, with AE = CD.

Prove that $\hat{B}_1 - \hat{B}_2 = \hat{A}_1$.
subQuestions.memoText:
Let $\hat{D}_1 = x$.
$\therefore \hat{B}_2 = x$ (equal chords subtend equal angles; AE = CD).
Let $\hat{E}_1 = y$.
$\therefore \hat{B}_1 = y$ (exterior angle of cyclic quadrilateral $=$ interior opposite angle).
$\therefore \hat{A}_1 = y - x$ (exterior angle of $\triangle$ $=$ sum of interior opposite angles).
$\therefore \hat{B}_1 - \hat{B}_2 = y - x = \hat{A}_1$.

subQuestions.label: 13(c)
subQuestions.questionText:
P and Q are the centres of two circles. Circle P has a radius of 3 cm and circle Q has a radius of 5 cm. The two circles touch each other at T. AB is a common tangent to the circles at R and S.

Determine the length of RS.
subQuestions.memoText:
Draw a perpendicular from P to SQ; call it PU.
$UQ = 5 - 3 = 2$ cm.
$PQ = 3 + 5 = 8$ cm (P, T and Q are collinear).
$(PU)^2 = (PQ)^2 - (UQ)^2 = (8)^2 - (2)^2 = 60$ (Pythagoras).
$PU = \sqrt{60} \approx 7{,}7$ cm.
$PU = RS$ (PRSU is a rectangle — $PR \perp AB$ and $QS \perp AB$, radii $\perp$ tangent).
$\therefore RS = \sqrt{60} \approx 7{,}7$ cm

subQuestions.label: 14(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Rectangle EBCF is inscribed in a semicircle with centre O and radius 8 cm, with E and F on the diameter. $B\hat{O}C = 2\theta$.

If the perimeter of the rectangle EBCF is represented by $P$, show that $P = 16\cos\theta + 32\sin\theta$.
subQuestions.memoText:
In $\triangle BOC$: $\hat{C} = 90° - \theta$ (isosceles $\triangle$; radii OB = OC; interior angles of $\triangle$).
In $\triangle OCF$: $\hat{C}_2 = \theta$.
$\dfrac{CF}{8} = \cos\theta \Rightarrow CF = 8\cos\theta$; $OF = 8\sin\theta$.
$P = 2 \times CF + 4 \times OF = 2(8\cos\theta) + 4(8\sin\theta)$
$\therefore P = 16\cos\theta + 32\sin\theta$

subQuestions.label: 14(b)
subQuestions.questionText: If it is further given that $P = 16\sqrt{5}\sin(\theta + \alpha)$ and $\alpha$ is an acute angle, determine the value of $\alpha$.
subQuestions.memoText:
$16\sqrt{5}\sin(\theta + \alpha) = 16\sqrt{5}\sin\theta\cos\alpha + 16\sqrt{5}\cos\theta\sin\alpha$
Comparing with $16\cos\theta + 32\sin\theta$:
$16\sqrt{5}\sin\alpha = 16$  and  $16\sqrt{5}\cos\alpha = 32$
$\tan\alpha = \dfrac{16}{32} = \dfrac{1}{2}$
$\alpha \approx 26{,}6°$
